items: A dictionary in Python is like a list in that it holds indexed values
Unlike a list, a dictionary doesn't use integer-based index values
Instead, dictionaries use immutable objects (like Strings) to index their content
In other languages dictionaries are often referred to as "associative arrays" or "hashmaps"

segments.html: Both dictionaries and lists are mutable (unlike strings)
segments.text: Both dictionaries and lists are mutable (unlike strings)

segments.html: But lists have an inherent order in which the objects are stored and dictionaries do not
segments.text: But lists have an inherent order in which the objects are stored and dictionaries do not

segments.html: List indeces are integers, but dictionary indeces can be any immutable object, like a string or an integer.
segments.text: List indeces are integers, but dictionary indeces can be any immutable object, like a string or an integer.

segments.html: Dictionary indeces are called "keys."
segments.text: Dictionary indeces are called "keys."

segments.html: Following is a sample dictionary with one integer key and two string keys. The objects indexed by the keys are called values.
segments.text: Following is a sample dictionary with one integer key and two string keys. The objects indexed by the keys are called values.

# create an empty dictionary
d={}
# set some values given keys
d[1]="hello"
d["joe"]=4
d["maria"]=5
# print the dictionary
print(d)
# print the keys
print(d.keys())
# print the values
print(d.values())

exercise.prompt:
Read the csv file, countries.csv, which contains the following fields on each line.

Country

Continent

GDP per capita

Population

Area

Gini

Read this data into a dictionary where the countries are the keys and the values are the populations. Then use this dictionary to print out the first 10 countries in alphabetical order and the ten least populous countries. And use it to print out the total population of the world.

Skip those countries with missing population; that is, don't include them in the dictionary.
